biggest_catch: This is a 2-year alcohol/cannabis behavior study: you wear an alcohol-sensor bracelet for a full month each year and answer daily app surveys about your drinking and drug use — pay is per completed portion and you can be withdrawn for low survey compliance.
catches: Not everyone qualifies: must be 18-29 and drink alcohol; if you complete under 75% of app surveys in week 1 the researchers may withdraw you, and continued low compliance can lead to exclusion

Data risk: no drugs or medical procedures (non-invasive), but you wear a biosensor bracelet continuously for a month each year and provide detailed alcohol and cannabis use data to the researchers — consider data privacy before enrolling

Time commitment: a little over 2 years total, with three separate month-long daily data-collection bursts (daily app surveys + continuous bracelet wear), plus onboarding/training sessions and annual online surveys

Location-specific: run by Brown University School of Public Health (Providence, RI); the study includes in-person staff meetings and equipment drop-offs, so local/regional access is likely needed — confirm with the study team whether remote participation is possible
Paid per completed portion (reloadable ClinCard debit or Amazon gift card); weekly survey pay depends on compliance tier, so low completion earns less

steps: Go to the official Brown Project ARC page and review the study description, timeline, and compensation
Contact the study team at ProjectARC@brown.edu or 401-863-2485 to enroll
Complete the onboarding session and first annual online survey
Complete each month-long burst: wear the alcohol-sensor bracelet continuously and answer daily app surveys about alcohol and cannabis use
Complete the annual online survey and refresher training before Bursts 2 and 3
Receive payments per completed portion on a ClinCard debit card or Amazon gift card
timing: A little over 2 years total: onboarding session, then three annual month-long data-collection bursts (daily smartphone app surveys + continuous alcohol-sensor bracelet wear), each preceded by an online survey (~60-75 min) and training meeting.
